name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd
tagline: North-India multi-specialty hospital chain compounding beds and revenue at 35-50% with strong trusted-user coverage and a sharply improved working-capital profile - now trading on Advent/Aster takeover speculation at ~53x, with the growth-capex funding path still unresolved
business_overview: Yatharth operates a network of multi-specialty and super-specialty hospitals concentrated in the NCR / western-UP belt (Noida, Greater Noida, Noida Extension, Faridabad, Delhi Model Town, Jhansi, Agra, and an under-fit-out Gurugram unit). Census bed capacity is ~2,555 operational within a ~2,800+ footprint across 9 hospitals; management now targets ~5,000+ beds within ~2.5 years. Growth is a mix of brownfield expansion at mature hubs and bolt-on acquisitions (Faridabad, Model Town Delhi, Agra's Shantived, Gurugram).
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 9,674 Cr (mid-cap); CMP ~Rs 1,002 (new all-time high on M&A reports)
~12.4% / ~10.4% (consolidated FY26) - low during the capital-intensive ramp

FY26 consol revenue Rs 1,207 Cr (+36-40%), EBITDA Rs 292 Cr (OPM 24%, down from 29% in FY24 on new-hospital drag), PAT Rs 170 Cr (+30%); Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 392.7 Cr (+51% YoY), EBITDA Rs 91.7 Cr (23.3% reported / 28.1% adjusted), PAT Rs 45.4 Cr (+8%)
Borrowings ~Rs 264 Cr (FY26); FY26 OCF ~Rs 205 Cr (company cites Rs 287 Cr, 98% conversion) but FY26 FCF -Rs 112 Cr on heavy capex
WC days 131 (FY24) -> 109 -> 80 (FY26); debtor days 131 -> 113; govt-scheme mix ~35%, targeted to ~25% over 2 years
~53x trailing P/E, ~28x EV/EBITDA - recent move partly an M&A/takeover premium
fundamentals_narrative: The growth engine is intact and executing: FY26 consolidated revenue +36-40% to Rs 1,207 Cr, PAT +30% to Rs 170 Cr, and a Q1 FY27 that grew 51% YoY with group occupancy 68% (up 7 ppt) and ARPOB Rs 34,758 (+6.7%). New units are ramping faster than the industry norm - Faridabad Sector-20 hit EBITDA breakeven in ~9 months, Agra delivered a 20%+ EBITDA margin in its first full quarter, Model Town breakeven is guided for H2 FY27. The working-capital story has genuinely improved: WC days fell from 131 (FY24) to 80 (FY26), debtor days to 113, with a stated push to cut the ~35% government-scheme mix toward ~25%. The two unresolved issues: (1) funding - management says the ~Rs 1,400 Cr bed-addition plan will be met from internal accrual with 'no fresh loans planned', but FY26 FCF was -Rs 112 Cr and borrowings are already ~Rs 264 Cr, so the maths is tight; (2) the promoter - after a Nov-2025 discounted open-market sale of 5.85%, late-Aug-2026 media reports say Advent International and Aster DM are in due diligence for a controlling stake (company denied being in sale talks). The stock has run to a new high of ~Rs 1,000 on that speculation, at ~53x earnings.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Stock broke out to a fresh all-time high (~Rs 1,000, first 4-digit print) on 28-Aug-2026 on the Advent/Aster controlling-stake reports; previously mid-range in a Rs 538-919 band.

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium-High -> Medium-High. Fundamental execution strengthened (Q1 FY27 +51%, faster new-unit breakevens, WC days 131->80), which offsets the persistent negative FCF and the unresolved capex-funding path. But the late-Aug M&A reports turn the stock into a partly binary situation at ~53x earnings, and the reported willingness to sell control (denied) deepens the promoter-commitment concern - so conviction holds rather than rises. Thesis-fit cut to 'neither': at Rs 9,700 Cr, ~35-40% growth and a 53x multiple already inflated by a takeover premium, a literal 10x in 2-3 years is not defensible.

sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 229 posts (Aug 2025 to Aug 2026). Sentiment is constructively bullish and unusually well-documented: trusted user ranvir (elevated) posted detailed results-and-concall notes for every quarter from Q1 FY26 through Q1 FY27, consistently framing 30%+ growth as on-track. Debate centered on (a) the Sep 2025 Agra (Shantived) acquisition at ~Rs 1.7 Cr/bed - initially called 'insane' vs prior ~Rs 0.5 Cr/bed deals, but the thread largely reconciled it as a ready 250-bed empanelled asset (it has since delivered a 20%+ EBITDA margin in its first full quarter); (b) the Nov 2025 promoter (Neena Tyagi) open-market sale of 5.85% at ~10% below CMP, which knocked the stock ~10% and drew 'immature promoter' criticism; (c) whether the ~Rs 1,500 Cr capex can be self-funded (MrBisht and drjpatwa flagged likely debt/dilution). CGHS/Ayushman rate revisions and oncology (~10% of revenue, +50% YoY) are recurring positive threads. The late-Aug-2026 Advent/Aster controlling-stake reports post-date most of the thread window.
community_signal: ranvir (trusted, elevated) is effectively the thread's analyst-of-record and remains a holder but stated he will not increase portfolio weight because of the government-mix working-capital drag. drjpatwa (trusted, elevated) endorsed the growth execution but flagged that debt and interest cost 'will need watching' now that the IPO/QIP cushion is largely spent. Maheshcm (trusted) was surprised by the Agra deal economics. Net: engaged trusted coverage leaning positive on execution, explicitly cautious on the funding path - and now with an M&A overlay the thread has not yet fully digested.

verdict_headline: A high-quality, fast-compounding hospital platform with best-in-class trusted-user coverage and a much-improved working-capital profile - but now a partly binary M&A situation at ~53x, and the growth-capex funding path is still unresolved
verdict_reasoning: Recent-quarter execution is unambiguously strong (Q1 FY27 revenue +51%, new hospitals breaking even faster than industry norms, WC days 131 -> 80) - the operating thesis is intact and, if anything, better than the prior write-up
Thesis-fit downgraded from 10x-in-2-3-years to 'neither': at Rs 9,700 Cr, ~35-40% growth and a 53x multiple already carrying a takeover premium, a literal 10x in 2-3 years is not a defensible label

Conviction held at Medium-High (not raised, not cut): stronger fundamentals are offset by an unresolved capex-funding path, a reported willingness of the promoter to sell control (denied), and a valuation now driven by M&A speculation
No red flag; revisit in ~30 days for any Advent/Aster deal confirmation or denial, the funding decision, and the Q2 FY27 print
